card.name: Sarandunga
card.era: Colonial-era cofradia roots; annual feast of St John the Baptist (late June)
card.tagline: Bani's Afro-Dominican drum-dance devotion to St. John the Baptist.
card.profile: The Sarandunga is a three-part complex of Afro-Dominican music and dance performed by the cofradia (brotherhood) of San Juan Bautista in and near Bani for the saint's late-June feast. The ensemble is unusual: three small double-headed laced-goatskin drums plus one guira, mostly in lively 6/8 - unlike the long-drum palos of the wider region. Subgenres include capitana, jacana and bomba rhythms, plus the morano (sung in quatrains, played in procession and at the altar). The festival climaxes before dawn with a procession of banner, saint and drums to the Bani River, where St. John's red banner blesses the water. The dance follows the baile de palos pattern but the male role is far more virtuosic, twirling a red handkerchief (Bloomsbury Music and Sound; Lameca).
card.insight: Per the Lameca ethnographic study, the morano appears to represent a syncretism between the ancient Canary Island drum dance (tajaraste) and Central-African influences, and the community preserves Sarandunga without help from folklorists or outside cultural groups.
